templates.system: You are a scene architect. Plan one scene as a short sequence of segments before any prose is written. Answer with ONE JSON object and nothing else.
templates.ask: Plan this scene as {min}-{max} segments of about {words} words in total. The first opens in motion, inside the point-of-view character's goal; the middle escalates the conflict; one segment lands the turn; the last ends on a hook into what comes next. Point of view and characters come only from the characters present in this scene. Answer with ONE JSON object:
templates.shapeNote: Role is one of opening, escalation, turn, hook. Each purpose above is only a start taken from this scene's description: write your own purpose for every segment as ONE short sentence, at most one, saying what happens in it and what it changes in this scene. A purpose is a plan line, not prose to copy into the story. EndsOn is where that segment cuts to the next one, as something on the page that the reader sees or hears: one action, one spoken line or one image, not a thought or a feeling (for the last segment, the scene's final moment). EndsOnKind says which it is: action, dialogue or image. Words is that segment's word target. Use only real names of the characters present.
templates.retry: Your previous answer was incomplete: give at least {min} segments, each with a purpose.
templates.retryPlaceholders: Do not copy the format's example values or any <...> placeholder: every segment needs its own purpose and real character names.
templates.previousScene: Previous scene (already written; do not repeat it): {title} — {summary}
templates.nextSegment: Next segment (do not write it; this one hands off to it): {purpose}
templates.tailHeading: The text so far ends like this. It is for continuity only: continue directly from it, do not repeat it, and do not imitate how it ends:
templates.prefillLead: The scene so far is already written at the start of your answer, inside <prose>. Continue it with this segment, in the same voice, as if there were no break; do not repeat it.
templates.soFarHeading: The scene so far. Your segment comes right after it: continue from its last line, in the same voice, as if there were no break; do not repeat it:
templates.write: Write segment {number} of {count} only: {purpose}. About {words} words.
templates.writeRole.OPENING: Open in motion: start inside the action, not with a summary or the weather.
templates.writeRole.ESCALATION: Raise the pressure: the conflict gets harder or more personal.
templates.writeRole.TURN: Land the turn: something shifts and the situation is no longer what it was.
templates.writeRole.HOOK: End the scene on a hook that pulls into what comes next; do not summarise or reflect.
templates.writeRules: Write only this segment's prose: no headings, no segment numbers, no recap of earlier text, and do not write later segments.
templates.stopOn.ACTION: Stop on this action, as it happens: {moment}.
templates.stopOn.DIALOGUE: Stop on this line, as it is spoken: {moment}.
templates.noConclusion: This is not the end of the scene: do not conclude, summarise, reflect or look ahead. End mid-story on an action, a line of dialogue or an image.
templates.landScene: This is the scene's last segment: land the scene.
